title: Small monoidal models of tensor-closed full subcategories
statement: Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and local and essential smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], full subcategories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and nonsymmetric monoidal infinity categories and strong monoidal functors of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a monoidal infinity category with locally $\mathcal U$-small underlying category $\mathcal V$. Let $D\subseteq\mathcal V$ be a replete full essentially $\mathcal U$-small subcategory containing the tensor unit and satisfying $x\otimes y\in D$ for all $x,y\in D$. Let $D^\otimes\subseteq\mathcal V^\otimes$ be the full subcategory on the objects over $[n]$ whose $n$ inert projections lie in $D$. Then $D^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a monoidal infinity category, and its inclusion preserves all cocartesian edges. There exist a $\mathcal U$-small monoidal infinity category $C^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and an equivalence $C^\otimes\simeq D^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving cocartesian edges. On the fibers over $[1]$ the composite defines a fully faithful strong monoidal functor $j:C\to\mathcal V$ with replete essential image $D$.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final sentence of proof (inherit cocartesian morphisms); Remark 7.17 (small monoidal model). General full-subcategory form of that construction; small replacement uses HTT Proposition 5.4.1.7 and Theorem 3.2.0.1. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion; archives WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Write $S=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, $E=D^\otimes$, and $q=p|_E$. A full subcategory has exactly the simplices whose vertices are in its object class. Hence every inner-horn lifting problem for $q$ has an ambient filler all of whose vertices already belong to $E$; this filler lies in $E$. Thus $q$ is an inner fibration and $E$ is a quasicategory. For two objects of $E$, their right-pinched mapping simplicial sets in $E$ and in $\mathcal V^\otimes$ are identical. Restrict the ambient Segal equivalence at $[n]$ to the full subcategories with all coordinates in $D$. An ambient quasi-inverse sends $D^n$ to $E_{[n]}$, since its inert projections are equivalent to the input coordinates and $D$ is replete; the unit and counit also restrict by fullness. Consequently $E_{[n]}\simeq D^n$. This includes $E_{[0]}\simeq *$ and $E_{[1]}=D$, since the only projection at $[1]$ is its identity.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final proof paragraph, and Remark 7.17; general restriction argument expanded by the agent

proof.text: For a base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, put $a=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[m]\to[n]$. The coherent block formula of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence] says that its $i$th output is the tensor of the consecutive list $x_{a(i-1)+1},\ldots,x_{a(i)}$. Each such output belongs to $D$: induct on the length of the list, using the unit for length zero, the input for length one, and binary tensor closure for the induction step. Repleteness removes the choices of Segal identifications and parenthesization. For $m=0$ the target is automatically in $E_{[0]}$. Therefore every ambient cocartesian lift with source in $E$ has target in $E$. This uses the block formula for arbitrary base arrows, including empty blocks and discarded initial or final inputs, rather than assuming only active arrows occur.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final proof paragraph, and Remark 7.17; general restriction argument expanded by the agent

proof.text: Take an ambient cocartesian lift $v:x\to z$ of any base arrow with $x\in E$. Its target lies in $E$ by step 2. Any outer-horn lifting problem that tests cocartesianness of $v$ for $q$ is an ambient lifting problem; its ambient filler has the prescribed vertices and hence lies in the full subcategory $E$. Thus $v$ is $q$-cocartesian. Since such a lift exists for every source and every outgoing base arrow, $q$ is a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final proof paragraph, and Remark 7.17; general restriction argument expanded by the agent

proof.text: Conversely, let $u:x\to y$ be any $q$-cocartesian edge over $\alpha$. Choose the ambient lift $v:x\to z$ of step 3. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to $q$: both $u$ and $v$ are initial in the same lift category $L(x,\alpha)$, so their universal comparison supplies an equivalence $h:z\to y$ in the target fiber and a triangle $hv\simeq u$. The inverse and its triangles remain in the ambient category by fullness. Precomposition with $h$ and with its inverse are homotopy inverse maps on ambient mapping spaces: associativity and the inverse triangles identify their composites with precomposition by identity edges, which is homotopic to the identity by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Its base arrow is the identity, so the mapping-space square for $h$ is a homotopy pullback. The criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes $h$ ambient cocartesian. The composition clause of the first cited node, applied now to $p$ and this triangle, makes $u$ ambient cocartesian. This proves that inclusion preserves every cocartesian edge, not just the chosen ambient lifts.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final proof paragraph, and Remark 7.17; general restriction argument expanded by the agent

proof.text: The Segal equivalences were proved in step 1. For the relative-limit axiom, choose any $q$-cocartesian inert projections out of $c\in E_{[n]}$. Step 4 makes them ambient cocartesian. For any test object $d\in E$ and any base arrow $\phi:p(d)\to[n]$, all mapping spaces and their maps to the base are identical to the ambient ones by fullness. Thus the ambient equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(d,c)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(d,c_i)$ is precisely the required equivalence in $E$. The empty product for $n=0$ is included. Together with step 3 this verifies every clause of the monoidal definition for $q$.

source.place: Proposition 7.15, final proof paragraph, and Remark 7.17; general restriction argument expanded by the agent

proof.text: The nerve $S$ is $\mathcal U$-small: the objects of $\Delta$ are the natural numbers, each morphism set consists of maps between finite ordered sets, and each set of finite strings of such maps is small. Each fiber $E_{[n]}\simeq D^n$ is essentially $\mathcal U$-small. Indeed an equivalence $D_0\simeq D$ with $D_0$ small, supplied by the hypothesis on $D$, gives the finite product equivalence $D_0^n\simeq D^n$, including $D_0^0=*$. Apply [lem-coef-small-cocartesian-model] to $q$ to obtain a small cocartesian fibration $r:C^\otimes\to S$ and an equivalence $F:C^\otimes\to E$ over $S$, preserving cocartesian edges and inducing equivalences $F_{[n]}$ on all fibers. No assumption that the original total simplicial set $E$ was already small is used.

source.place: Remark 3.3.2.3, property (*′), cocartesian dual, and Theorem 3.2.0.1; universe reduction isolated in lem-coef-small-cocartesian-model, applied to the small-model assertion underlying Chu–Haugseng Remark 7.17

proof.text: Set $C=C^\otimes_{[1]}$. Because $F$ preserves cocartesian inert edges, its fiber equivalences identify the Segal map for $C^\otimes$ with the Segal map for $E$, giving $C^\otimes_{[n]}\simeq C^n$. The total equivalence $F$ induces mapping-space equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. These lie over the same discrete base mapping sets, so they induce equivalences on the fibers over each base arrow; a weak equivalence over a discrete set is a weak equivalence on each of its components over that set. The relative-limit formulas of step 5 therefore give exactly the relative-limit formulas for $C^\otimes$. Hence $r$ is monoidal. The composite $C^\otimes\xrightarrow F E\hookrightarrow\mathcal V^\otimes$ preserves all cocartesian edges by steps 4 and 6, so its restriction $j:C\to\mathcal V$ is strong monoidal. Its fiber factor $C\xrightarrow{F_{[1]}}D$ is an equivalence and $D\hookrightarrow\mathcal V$ is full, so $j$ is fully faithful; its essential image is exactly the given replete $D$.
